description: We are the AstroNex Team, a group of curious and creative students passionate about space exploration, science, and technology. Guided by our supervisor, we aim to explore human survival on Mars through innovative ideas, research, teamwork, and problem-solving. We welcome enthusiastic members with skills in science, coding, research, creativity, and design who are eager to learn, collaborate, and think beyond Earth! 🚀
summary:
Marswalk Mission navigation map and survival dashboard designed to support future astronaut exploration of Jezero Crater.
Our project brings together eight different map layers, including elevation, temperature, mineral information and radiation, allowing users to explore important scientific data in one place. It also helps identify suitable exploration routes, preview surface conditions, and highlight potential hazards such as steep slopes, loose sand and dust storms.
In addition, the dashboard includes an oxygen and battery tracking system to help astronauts monitor their resources and plan their return. Scientific waypoints connect important locations to exploration goals, such as collecting rock samples and investigating evidence of ancient water.
By combining navigation, scientific information and resource planning, our project aims to make Mars exploration more informed, organized and efficient.
details:
MarsWalk Mission is a real-time, human-centric navigation and life-support dashboard designed for astronauts conducting Extravehicular Activities (EVAs) on Mars. The system works by blending eight core NASA planetary data streams—such as topographic elevation (MOLA), mineralogy (CRISM), and thermal mapping (THEMIS)—into a single, unified interface. Operating entirely offline without GPS, it relies on inertial suit sensors and visual terrain-matching while continuously tracking live suit telemetry, including oxygen, battery power, suit pressure, and core body temperature. At the same time, its built-in EVA Budget calculator dynamically monitors walking speed and protects emergency backup supplies to guarantee astronauts can always make it safely back to base.

The primary benefit of MarsWalk Mission is its ability to reduce cognitive load for astronauts wearing bulky pressurized spacesuits under high-stress conditions. Rather than forcing crew members to interpret dense numbers or juggle multiple tools, the dashboard translates complex environmental and life-support data into instant, glance-and-go visual cues—using green for safe paths, yellow for moderate risk, and red for NO-GO hazards. By uniting route planning, terrain hazard detection, and life-support monitoring on one screen, the project aims to bridge the gap between orbital science and surface survival, enabling human explorers in places like Jezero Crater to collect samples and search for signs of ancient life rapidly without compromising crew safety.

To develop the project, our team utilized Figma to design the human-centric UI/UX dashboard interface, alongside Python and scientific libraries such as NumPy, Matplotlib, and rasterio to process and layer open-source NASA orbital datasets.  From a hardware perspective, the interface is conceptualized for a chest-mounted or wrist-cuff display supported by hands-free voice commands and audio alerts. What makes MarsWalk Mission especially creative is how it flips the perspective of existing planetary mapping tools: while platforms like NASA’s Mars Trek are built for scientists sitting at desks on Earth, MarsWalk acts as an active field co-pilot engineered for human ergonomics, offline Martian physics, steep 15-degree slope limits, and strict emergency resource margins.
